fit_line: A remote-in-India full-stack seat where "Use AI tools to accelerate coding, debugging, refactoring, testing, documentation, and delivery workflows" is the job, and Hussain brings React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, end-to-end API tests and daily Claude Code use.
ai_in_job: "Use AI tools to accelerate coding, debugging, refactoring, testing, documentation, and delivery workflows"; also "Apply judgment in verifying AI outputs, identifying hallucinations, and protecting code quality" and "This is not an AI research or ML engineering role."

screening_answers.question: Why are you interested in this role and Betterworks?
screening_answers.answer: The role treats AI-assisted development as the normal way to work while still holding engineers to correctness, testing and maintainability. That is how I already work. I have spent 3 years as a full-stack developer, and I use Claude Code every day. I also like that it is a product engineering role on an enterprise SaaS platform, with features owned from design to production readiness.

screening_answers.question: How do you use AI coding tools across the development lifecycle?
screening_answers.answer: I use Claude Code daily. I plan the work first, scaffold with the agent, have it draft tests, then review every diff by hand before it goes in. I hold Anthropic's Claude Code in Action and Claude Code 101 certifications. I have not used Cursor or GitHub Copilot as my main tools, but the habits carry over: give the tool clear context, check its output, and keep ownership of the design.

screening_answers.question: How do you verify AI-generated output and avoid over-trusting it?
screening_answers.answer: In PageForge, my account-based marketing page generator, the AI drafts only from approved facts. A deterministic validator then flags unsupported numbers, and a reviewer signs off claim by claim before anything is published. In multi-agent-research-crew, a verifier agent does claim-level citation checking. I apply the same rule to code: fluent output is still a draft, and review is the bottleneck, not generation.

screening_answers.question: Describe a project you own end to end, including testing.
screening_answers.answer: Orbital Surplus (orbital-surplus.vercel.app) is a full-stack store, a fictional demo brand running Stripe in test mode. Stock holds are race-safe: one transaction with a conditional UPDATE, so only one shopper wins the last unit. Payment confirmation is idempotent, whether it arrives through the return page or a signed Stripe webhook. It has 9 end-to-end API tests. Node 20 and Postgres (Neon) on the back end. My portfolio site (hussain-singapuri.vercel.app) has a booking backend with 10 end-to-end API tests.

screening_answers.question: Do you have experience with Vue, NestJS, Django, AWS or Kubernetes?
screening_answers.answer: Not with Vue, NestJS, Django, AWS or Kubernetes. My front end is React 19 and Next.js, my back end is Node.js and FastAPI with REST APIs, and I use Docker and GitHub Actions for delivery. I would ramp up on Vue from my React experience, since the component model is similar.

screening_answers.question: What is your expected salary?
screening_answers.answer: I am targeting INR 30,000 per month or more. I am flexible on structure; the work and the total package matter to me. [CONFIRM: whether to give a figure or ask Betterworks for the band first, since the posting states no salary.]

screening_answers.question: What is your notice period / earliest start date?
screening_answers.answer: Immediate. My previous role ended in September 2026.

screening_answers.question: Where are you based, and are you comfortable with remote, async work?
screening_answers.answer: I am based in Pune, India (IST, UTC+05:30). I worked remotely for a US-based medical-device company for 3 years, so remote and async work across time zones is familiar, and I am happy to overlap with US mornings.
